doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York clubs and the Embers trio
title: Boston musicians: John Neves, Alan Dawson and Sidney Catlett's rent party
summary: She remembers bassist John Neves, whom she found temperamental, meeting Alan Dawson only years later at Boston clubs, and attending a rent party for Sidney Catlett.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Excellent, excellent. There was one . . . a couple of little sidebars I just wanted . . . Did you meet musicians like John Neves and Alan Dawson at that time too?
Oh yes. But it’s funny. I did not meet Alan Dawson. I don’t know why I didn’t. But I met John Neves. Didn’t he have a brother . . .
Brother Paul Neves.
Paul Neves. Didn’t he die?
Yes he did.

John worked with me at one point later on, after I’d been in the Hickory House. I really loved his playing. He worked with me in St. Louis . . . other places too. But not for long. He was tempermental.
Yeah.
He really was tough to get along with.
I didn’t know him at that period of course. And Alan may have been out with Lionel Hampton at that particular time, so that may have . . .

I don’t know. I didn’t meet Alan until much later, years later. I would go up to Boston. Played at the Jazz Workshop. I think I took my own trio at that time. I think I took Michael Moore, but then I . . . later I did play with Alan at a place called the Stardust Room, which was . . .
No, the Starlight.
Starlight Room. It was owned by . . .
Starlight Roof. It was on . . .
No. Well, yes, and this was owned by this guy that married Carol Sloane, Bucky . . .
Right, yeah, Buck . . .
Bucky something.
Buck Spur.
Buck Spur, right.
Oh, that’s much later. That’s even during my time, had a little . . .
Oh really. That was not . . . I guess I mention that because of Alan. It was not too much before that that I met Alan Dawson. I don’t know how I escaped meeting him. There would be different circles.
Oh yes.

Still, in a way I guess I was still more involved with the people that Jimmy would have. And then I met . . . I’m having to go back to Chicago . . . Sidney Catlett and people like that. Anyway, he was in Boston at the time, and he had a rent party that we all went to.
Yeah, I’d like to see a few of those right now. [laughs]
I forget whose rent we were paying. Probably his.
